source.stem:
A ball is dropped from a table-top. Air resistance may be ignored.
Which row describes the velocity and the acceleration of the ball at point X?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The object's mass on the Moon is less because gravity is weaker there.

mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Use grams or kilograms for mass and newtons for weight.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: same mass; different planetary gravitational force -> different weight happens first, and that produces same amount of matter.

intelligence.enrichment: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and is measured in grams or kilograms; its value remains the same at every place. Weight depends on gravitational force, so an object's weight can be different on different planets even when its mass remains the same. same amount of matter -> same mass; different planetary gravitational force -> different weight The learner correctly applies this rule: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and is measured in grams or kilograms; its value remains the same at every place. Weight depends on gravitational force, so an object's weight can be different on different planets even when its mass remains the same. Mass and weight are two words for the same number, so changing planet should not change either one.
